title.en: US strikes on Iran reportedly hit airport and bridges – Middle East crisis live
title.zh: 美国对伊朗的袭击据报击中机场和桥梁——中东危机实时报道

summary.en: Reports indicate US strikes hit an airport and bridges in Iran, while Iranian media claims the IRGC destroyed US fighter jets in Jordan. US marines boarded a tanker amid a blockade of Iranian ports, and Kuwait reported an attack on its power and water desalination plant by Iran.
summary.zh: 据报道，美国对伊朗的袭击击中了机场和桥梁，而伊朗媒体称伊斯兰革命卫队摧毁了驻扎在约旦的美国战斗机。在伊朗港口被封锁之际，美国海军陆战队登上一艘油轮，科威特能源部表示其一座电力和海水淡化厂遭到伊朗袭击。

body.en: Southern rail station also attacked, Iranian media says, as IRGC claims to have destroyed US fighter jets stationed in Jordan US marines board tanker amid blockade of Iranian ports Kuwait’s energy ministry said one of its power and water desalination plants was attacked by Iran, resulting in a fire and damage to the facility. In a statement shared online, the country’s ministry of electricity, water and renewable energy said emergency services were able to control and extinguish the fire, while technical teams worked to restore service and monitor the electricity grid. Six bridges in Khamir county in Hormozgan province were hit, resulting in the deaths of seven people. One person was killed in the port city of Bandar Abbas in Hormozgan province, where several areas were struck by missiles including a railway station The maritime control tower of Shahid Kalantari port in Chabahar in Sistan and Baluchestan province was targeted for a third time and “completely destroyed”. No casualties were reported. Continue reading...
body.zh: 伊朗媒体称，伊朗南部火车站也遭到袭击，伊朗革命卫队声称摧毁了驻扎在约旦的美国战斗机，美国海军陆战队在伊朗港口封锁期间登上油轮。科威特能源部表示，其一处电力和海水淡化厂遭到伊朗袭击，导致设施起火和损坏。在网上分享的一份声明中，该国电力、水利和可再生能源部表示，紧急服务能够控制并扑灭大火，而技术团队则致力于恢复服务并监控电网。霍尔木兹甘省哈米尔县6座桥梁被击中，造成7人死亡。霍尔木兹甘省港口城市阿巴斯港造成一人死亡，包括火车站在内的多个地区遭到导弹袭击。锡斯坦和俾路支斯坦省恰巴哈尔省沙希德·卡兰塔里港海事控制塔第三次成为袭击目标并“被彻底摧毁”。没有人员伤亡报告。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The escalating reports of strikes and counter-claims in the Middle East highlight the dangerous cycle of retaliation. In such moments, Yahweh's word reminds us not to be overcome by evil, but to seek ways to overcome evil with good. This calls for a different kind of strength, one that resists the urge to mirror aggression and instead pursues paths of peace.
reflection.zh: 中东地区不断升级的袭击和反击报道，凸显了危险的报复循环。在这样的时刻，雅伟的话语提醒我们不要被恶所胜，而要以善胜恶。这呼唤一种不同的力量，一种抵制以侵略回应侵略的冲动，转而寻求和平道路的力量。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

title.en: Burnham to say his government will be ‘unashamedly Labour’ in first speech as party leader – UK politics live
title.zh: 伯纳姆将在首次党魁演讲中称其政府将“毫不掩饰地工党化”——英国政治直播

summary.en: Andy Burnham is set to be formally announced as the new Labour leader at a special conference. Reports indicate that if he becomes Prime Minister, his government will allow more drilling in the North Sea, with officials exploring various policy options.
summary.zh: 安迪·伯纳姆将在一次特别会议上被正式宣布为工党新领袖。据报道，如果他成为首相，他的政府将允许在北海进行更多钻探，官员们正在研究各种政策方案。

body.en: ‘Special conference’ to take place at noon where Burnham will be formally announced as Labour leader Andy Burnham will reportedly allow more drilling in the North Sea when he becomes PM. A story for Bloomberg says: Officials are working on a range of options. They include signalling willingness to approve new oil and gas fields at Jackdaw and Rosebank, and an expansion of so-called tiebacks which allow further drilling on or near existing fields. No final decision has been made on what form the North Sea announcement will take, but Burnham is likely to indicate he is in favour of more drilling, the people said. Burnham has told Scottish Labour MPs that he will make an early visit to Aberdeen to underline the importance he attaches to the North Sea oil and gas industry. Gary Smith, leader of the GMB union, and Sharon Graham, leader of Unite the Union, have slammed the Labour government’s policy of ending new exploration licences in the basin on environmental grounds as “economic madness” and “an act of self-harm” respectively. Continue reading...
body.zh: 中午将举行“特别会议”，伯纳姆将被正式宣布为工党领袖。据报道，安迪·伯纳姆在成为首相后将允许在北海进行更多钻探。彭博社的一篇报道称：官员们正在研究一系列选择。其中包括表示愿意批准寒鸦和罗斯班克的新油气田，以及扩大所谓的回接，允许在现有油田或附近进一步钻探。知情人士称，目前尚未就北海公告将采取何种形式做出最终决定，但伯纳姆可能表示他赞成进行更多钻探。伯纳姆告诉苏格兰工党议员，他将提前访问阿伯丁，以强调他对北海石油和天然气行业的重视。 GMB工会领袖加里·史密斯（Gary Smith）和联合工会领袖莎朗·格雷厄姆（Sharon Graham）分别抨击工党政府以环境为由终止该盆地新勘探许可证的政策，称其为“经济疯狂”和“自残行为”。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As a new political leader prepares to outline his vision, the biblical call to "do justice and righteousness" offers a timeless guide for governance. This mandate reminds those in power to protect the vulnerable and ensure fairness for all citizens, establishing a throne not just by policy, but by moral integrity. May leaders be inspired to serve with a...
reflection.zh: 当一位新的政治领袖准备阐述其愿景时，圣经中“行公义，行正直”的呼召为治理提供了永恒的指引。这一诫命提醒掌权者要保护弱势群体，确保所有公民都享有公平，不仅通过政策，更通过道德正直来建立其权位。愿领袖们受感召，以一颗为公共利益服务的心来治理，特别是为寄居的、孤儿和寡妇。

verse.textEn: Do what is just and right. Rescue from the hand of the oppressor the one who has been robbed.
verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.en: US launches new strikes as Iran says civilian infrastructure hit
title.zh: 美国发动新一轮袭击，伊朗境内传出爆炸声

summary.en: The US has launched a new series of strikes targeting Iranian military capabilities, with reports of blasts in Iran. This marks the sixth consecutive day of fighting between the two sides.
summary.zh: 据报道，美国对伊朗军事目标发动了新一轮袭击，伊朗境内传出爆炸声。这已是双方连续第六天发生冲突。

body.en:
The US launched a wave of strikes against Iran for the sixth night in a row, its military said, as the two sides battled over control of the Strait of Hormuz.

US Central Command (Centcom) said the attacks were intended to "further degrade Iranian military capabilities", before saying it had boarded a vessel as part of its blockade of Iranian ports.

State media and provincial authorities reported that the US had hit civilian infrastructure, including bridges, a train station and an airport. BBC Verify has confirmed an attack on one bridge to the west of Bandar Abbas in Hormozgan province.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says it has retaliated by striking US maritime surveillance radar sites in Oman as well as targets in Kuwait and Bahrain. They also claim to have attacked a US special operations command centre in Syria.

The IRGC said the surprise attack at al-Tanf in Syria, near the border with Jordan, was in retaliation for the killing of Iranian soldiers two days ago. Neither Syria nor the US have commented on the claim.

Later on Friday, Jordan's military said it shot down three Iranian missiles with no casualties or damage reported.

The IRGC claimed it struck US fighter jets stationed in the Gulf country, according to state TV.

Meanwhile in Iraqi Kurdistan, eight people were killed and several injured in the city of Sulaymaniyah in the early morning, according to Kurdish news agency Rudaw and Agence France Press news agency. Kurdish forces blamed the attack on Iran.

Separately, Kuridsh forces said eight drones were also shot down over the city of Erbil, with no casualties reported.

As attacks escalate, the Strait of Hormuz - a critical waterway off Iran's coast that Tehran effectively blocked in response to US-Israeli strikes - has remained shut.

That has impacted the flow of oil from the region and the head of the International Energy Agency, Fatih Birol, says he has concerns about global energy supplies.

"We should be worried, and I am worried, if the situation does not improve in the next few weeks," Birol said on Thursday night.

On Friday the Chinese and Pakistani foreign ministers called for the US and Iran to stop fighting and resume negotiations.

The US overnight strikes also hit close to the island of Qeshm as well as in the southern coastal cities of Bandar Abbas and Bushehr - the site of a nuclear power plant.

Centcom did not mention bridges in its list of the "dozens of Iranian military targets" it hit in the latest round of strikes. It said jets, drones and ships had attacked "coastal surveillance and air defense sites, military logistics infrastructure, and maritime capabilities". The BBC has asked Centcom for comment.

body.zh: 美国军方表示，美国连续第六晚对伊朗发动新一波打击，双方仍在争夺霍尔木兹海峡的控制权。 美国中央司令部（Centcom）周四表示，这些袭击的目的是“进一步削弱伊朗的军事能力”。 伊朗官方媒体报道称，美国导弹袭击了靠近霍尔木兹海峡的海湾格什姆岛以及阿巴斯港和布什尔核电站所在地。 此前，双方隔夜交锋，新一轮的敌对行动进一步加剧了双方结束战争的初步协议。 白宫新闻秘书卡罗琳·莱维特周四表示，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普仍对与伊朗进行谈判持开放态度。 “当他们背弃对美国所说的话时，总统将追究他们的责任。但与此同时，他总是对外交持开放态度，”她告诉记者。 她说，伊朗已表示仍希望与美国达成协议，并补充道：“我们正在与他们交谈，但总统不会允许他们在不承担后果的情况下向海峡内的船只开火。” 随着袭击升级，霍尔木兹海峡仍然关闭。霍尔木兹海峡是伊朗海岸附近的一条重要水道，德黑兰为应对美以袭击而有效封锁了该海峡。 周四早些时候，德黑兰表示袭击了美国在约旦、科威特和巴林的军事基地，而美国则表示对海峡多个地点发动了长达六个小时的袭击。 在这些交流之前，特朗普警告伊朗，如果伊朗不重返谈判，它必须“表现得更好”，否则将面临进一步的军事行动。 伊朗最高谈判代表穆罕默德·巴格尔·加利巴夫对官方媒体表示，德黑兰“没有理由”遵守任何不利于该国的协议。 他补充说，伊朗的国家安全取决于维持他所说的霍尔木兹海峡的“伊朗安排”。 与此同时，特朗普周三赞扬伊朗释放了美国被拘留者德纳·卡拉里(Dena Karari)，他称德纳·卡拉里于2024年12月被“错误拘留”。 “美利坚合众国赞赏伊朗的这一善意姿态！”特朗普在《真相社会》上撰文。 然而，据伊朗官方媒体报道，伊朗司法部门周四表示，尚未从其监狱释放或交换任何美国囚犯。

reflection.en: The ongoing cycle of strikes and counter-strikes reminds us of the ancient warning that those who live by the sword often perish by it. In times of escalating conflict, this truth underscores the tragic consequences of continuous violence. It calls for a deeper reflection on how to break such destructive patterns.
reflection.zh: 持续的打击与反击循环，提醒我们古老的警示：凡动刀的，必死在刀下。在冲突升级的时刻，这一真理凸显了持续暴力的悲剧性后果。它呼吁我们更深地反思如何打破这种破坏性的模式。

verse.textEn: All who draw the sword will die by the sword.
verse.textZh: 凡动刀的，必死在刀下。

title.en: ICE arrests human rights lawyer who fled Chinese crackdown
title.zh: ICE逮捕了逃离中国镇压的人权律师

summary.en: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has arrested Wu Shaoping, a Chinese human rights lawyer awaiting an asylum decision in Pennsylvania. The arrest has raised concerns about his potential deportation to China, where he fears persecution.
summary.zh: 美国移民和海关执法局（ICE）在宾夕法尼亚州逮捕了正在等待庇护决定的中国人权律师吴绍平。此次逮捕引发了人们对其可能被遣返中国并面临迫害的担忧。

body.en: Arrest in Pennsylvania of Wu Shaoping, who is awaiting asylum decision, raises fears of deportation and persecution A Chinese human rights lawyer has been arrested by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), raising concerns he could be deported to China where he would face persecution. Wu Shaoping fled China at the end of 2019 amid a crackdown on human rights lawyers. He travelled to the US on a tourist visa and made an asylum claim in 2020, for which he is still awaiting a decision. Continue reading...
body.zh: 正在等待庇护决定的吴少平在宾夕法尼亚州被捕，引发了对驱逐出境和迫害的担忧一名中国人权律师被美国移民和海关执法局（ICE）逮捕，引发了人们的担忧，他可能会被驱逐到中国，在那里他将面临迫害。 2019年底，吴少平因人权律师遭到打压而逃离中国。他持旅游签证前往美国，并于 2020 年提出庇护申请，目前仍在等待决定。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news highlights the vulnerability of those seeking refuge and the moral imperative to treat foreigners with dignity and care. Yahweh's ancient command reminds us to welcome the stranger, remembering our shared humanity and the experiences of displacement. May compassion guide decisions concerning those who flee persecution in search of safety.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了寻求庇护者的脆弱性，以及以尊严和关怀对待外国人的道德责任。雅伟古老的诫命提醒我们欢迎陌生人，记住我们共同的人性和流离失所的经历。愿怜悯之心指引那些为寻求安全而逃离迫害之人的相关决定。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

The 22-year-old film graduate, who aspires to be an editor, made the journey from Atlanta to London to watch Christopher Nolan’s take on Homer’s epic poem, The Odyssey. Continue reading...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: Trump alleges China meddled in 2020 election and questions voting security ahead of midterms
title.zh: 特朗普在中期选举前指控美国选举安全存在“令人震惊的漏洞”

summary.en: The president has made claims about China's interference in the 2020 US election, which contradict previous findings from US intelligence agencies. These allegations come as the country prepares for upcoming midterm elections.
summary.zh: 总统声称中国干预了2020年美国大选，这与美国情报机构此前的调查结果直接矛盾。这些指控是在该国准备中期选举之际提出的。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has delivered a primetime address in which he accused China of interfering in the 2020 election and alleged "shocking vulnerabilities" in American voting systems.

Trump, who spoke from the White House on Thursday, has repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims about voter fraud and foreign meddling in the 2020 election, which he lost to Joe Biden.

In the half-hour speech, delivered three months before the midterm elections, he said he had declassified hundreds of intelligence files which supported his claims that Beijing had tried to sway the election in Biden's favour.

The US intelligence community has previously concluded China did not interfere in the 2020 election.

In response to his speech, China's foreign ministry strongly denied the allegations of Chinese meddling in the 2020 presidential election, saying they were "entirely fabricated".

Trump's claims are "malicious smears" which have "long been proven to be groundless", foreign ministry spokesman Lin Jian said.

Trump spoke in front of several members of his top team as he gave his address, but journalists were unable to put questions to the president.

In his remarks, he accused China of the "illicit acquisition" of 220 million voter files including personal information.

Trump said voter data in 18 states was "bought, stolen or hacked by China" and accused "those responsible for sounding the alarm" of not disclosing the discovery to government officials or Congress.

Trump did not in his speech present any evidence that China had used the information it allegedly gathered to alter voting systems or to influence election outcomes.

Hundreds of pages of intelligence documents were released by the White House during Trump's address, many of them heavily redacted. The BBC is in the process of reviewing them.

Democrats, meanwhile, accused Trump of attempting to sow doubts about the security of the upcoming November midterms which will decide control of Congress for the remainder of his presidency.

"Let's be clear - in America, voters choose their leaders, not the other way around," top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer posted on social media after the speech.

"Democrats will fight like hell to make sure every American voter can cast their ballot freely, without obstruction or interference from Donald Trump," he added.

The president's comments contradict previous US intelligence assessments. A 2021 report by the US National Intelligence Council said it had "high confidence" that China did not interfere in the 2020 presidential election.

"We assess that China did not deploy interference efforts and considered but did not deploy influence efforts intended to change the outcome of the US presidential election," the report stated.

title.en: China hits out at British Steel nationalisation
title.zh: 中国抨击英国钢铁国有化

summary.en: The UK government announced the nationalization of British Steel, stating the move was to protect a crucial national capability. China subsequently expressed strong disapproval of this decision.
summary.zh: 英国政府宣布将英国钢铁公司收归国有，称此举旨在维护“一项重要的国家能力”。中国随后对此决定表示强烈不满。

body.en:
China has hit out at the nationalisation of British Steel, saying it "firmly opposes and is strongly dissatisfied with the British government's decision".

On Thursday, the UK government said that taking the loss-making firm into public hands would protect jobs and safeguard a "vital national capability".

The UK took control of British Steel's operations in Scunthorpe last year, though it was still owned by China's Jingye Group, limiting the government's ability to steer its future.

China's commerce ministry said on Friday that the moves "seriously infringed upon Jingye's legitimate rights and interests and severely undermined the confidence of Chinese companies investing in the UK".

It also called on Britain to "faithfully fulfil" its obligations under the China–UK Bilateral Investment Treaty.

"Disregarding Jingye's significant contribution to the UK economy and society, the British side forcibly took control of the company in the name of national security," the ministry said.

The statement added that Beijing would monitor developments closely and support Chinese firms to protect their rights, but did not specify what protecting Chinese companies' rights might involve.

The decision to nationalise British Steel threatens to strain the relationship between London and Beijing just as Andy Burnham is set to become the prime minister on Monday.

The incoming PM will have to weigh his approach to the issue with the economic benefits of ties with the world's second largest economy.

The China-UK Bilateral Investment Treaty is a legally binding agreement that was signed in 1986. It was designed to promote and protect investments between the two countries.

The nationalisation came after Parliament on Wednesday passed legislation allowing the government to bring the steel industry into public ownership under circumstances where it met a public interest test.

Jingye is seeking compensation, having previously said the business was losing £700,000 a day. The BBC has been unable to get a response from Jingye itself to Thursday's announcement.

By taking British Steel into public ownership the government now has the power and freedom to decide on the future of the plant, while keeping the blast furnaces going.

It is unlikely the government will want to continue running the business in the long term as it is costing it more than a million pounds a day.

In March, the National Audit Office said the Scunthorpe steelworks was costing the government about £1.3m a day.

Business Secretary Peter Kyle told the BBC the government would need to cover the running costs "for the immediate future".

The steelworks directly employs around 2,700 people in Scunthorpe as well as supporting thousands more jobs in the supply chain.

body.zh: 中方对英国钢铁公司国有化予以猛烈抨击，称“坚决反对，对英国政府的决定表示强烈不满”。 周四，英国政府表示，将这家亏损公司纳入公众手中将保护就业并维护“重要的国家能力”。 英国去年控制了英国钢铁公司在斯肯索普的业务，尽管该公司仍由中国敬业集团所有，这限制了政府掌控其未来的能力。 中国商务部周五表示，此举“严重侵犯敬业公司的合法权益，严重损害中国企业对英国投资的信心”。 它还呼吁英国“忠实履行”中英双边投资条约规定的义务。 英方无视敬业公司对英国经济社会的重大贡献，以国家安全为名，强行控制敬业公司。 声明补充说，北京将密切关注事态发展并支持中国企业保护自身权利，但没有具体说明保护中国企业权利可能涉及哪些内容。 就在安迪·伯纳姆将于周一就任英国首相之际，英国钢铁公司国有化的决定可能会导致伦敦和北京之间的关系紧张。 即将上任的总理必须权衡自己处理这一问题的方法与与世界第二大经济体建立联系的经济利益。 《中英双边投资条约》是1986年签署的具有法律约束力的协议，旨在促进和保护两国之间的投资。 周三，议会通过了一项立法，允许政府在满足公共利益要求的情况下将钢铁行业纳入公有制。 敬业正在寻求赔偿，此前曾表示该业务每天损失 70 万英镑。 BBC 尚未得到敬业本身对周四的公告的回应。 通过将英国钢铁公司纳入公有制，政府现在拥有决定工厂未来的权力和自由，同时保持高炉的运转。 从长远来看，政府不太可能继续经营该业务，因为每天的成本超过一百万英镑。 3 月份，国家审计办公室表示，斯肯索普钢铁厂每天给政府造成的损失约为 130 万英镑。 商务大臣彼得·凯尔告诉英国广播公司，政府需要“在不久的将来”承担运营成本。

title.en: Mandela Day: Has South Africa failed his vision?
title.zh: 曼德拉日：南非是否辜负了他的愿景？

summary.en: Three decades after the end of apartheid, many South Africans believe that Nelson Mandela's vision for the nation remains unrealized. Persistent issues such as inequality, xenophobia, and anti-migrant protests continue to challenge the legacy he left behind.
summary.zh: 种族隔离结束三十年后，许多南非人认为纳尔逊·曼德拉的国家愿景仍未实现。不平等、仇外心理和反移民抗议等持续存在的问题，继续考验着他留下的遗产。

body.en:
Three decades after apartheid, many South Africans say Nelson Mandela's vision remains unfulfilled. Inequality, xenophobia and anti-migrant protests continue to test his legacy.

In South Africa, Nelson Mandela is honored every year on July 18, the birthday of the former president and Nobel Peace Prize laureate. On Mandela Day, people around the world are encouraged to help build a more just society.

South Africa's anti-apartheid hero fought against discrimination based on skin color and ethnicity. Yet three decades after the end of apartheid, many Africans in South Africa still face xenophobia, rejection and violence.

"We live in a world where many young people feel hopeless because opportunities are limited, and frustrations are easily directed at foreigners, who are often seen as competitors for jobs," said Mpho Tsotetsi, a 32-year-old South African social worker who lives in a township near Johannesburg.

Nevertheless, she does not see Mandela's dream as shattered forever, but admits it has been challenged. "Mandela envisioned a South Africa built on reconciliation, respect for human dignity, and African solidarity," Tsotetsi told DW.

Mandela was aware that many African countries stood by South Africa in the struggle against apartheid, according to Tsotetsi. "He believed that Africa's future depended on unity rather than division."

Many migrants have fled South Africa in recent weeks out of fear — vigilante groups such as "March and March" and "Operation Dudula" have threatened further violence and intimidated people.

According to Tsotetsi, the recent "Mabahambe" ("You must go!") march and wider  anti-migrant protests  reflect the frustration of many South Africans who believe the government has failed to tackle unemployment, crime, irregular migration and poor service delivery. Critics, however, have described the protests as xenophobic .

According to Verne Harris, a staff member and former archivist for Nelson Mandela at the Mandela Foundation, these  frustrations among the population are legitimate.

People are growing impatient, but the demonstrations are also politically driven. With local elections approaching in November, opposition parties have an incentive to stoke anti-government sentiment.

"Nelson Mandela's legacy is not a static thing, but a dynamic public resource open to new interpretations," Harris told DW. "It has been always been made and remade over time; it is a living thing. It can be mobilized for good, also for evil."

Madiba, as Mandela was popularly known, spoke publicly for the first time about Afrophobia and xenophobia of all kinds shortly after taking office as the country's president in 1994, according to Harris.

title.en: Why Pauline Hanson's appearance on Tommy Robinson's podcast is so controversial
title.zh: 为什么波琳·汉森出现在汤米·罗宾逊的播客上如此有争议

summary.en: Pauline Hanson's podcast with a far-right UK activist has sparked backlash — and a defence from Barnaby Joyce.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has drawn criticism for appearing on a podcast with controversial far-right UK activist Tommy Robinson, where she pointed to the scrapping of the White Australia policy as the root cause of migration issues in the country.

The nearly hour-long conversation, recorded last week during Hanson's visit to the UK, was published on Robinson's podcast on Friday.

The appearance has since drawn criticism from other politicians, though not everyone in Canberra has condemned it.

Between speaking about her scepticism about the COVID-19 vaccine, the potential for her daughter to eventually lead One Nation, and reflections on her time in prison and her burqa incidents in parliament , Hanson focused heavily on immigration.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Asked by Robinson how Australia had ended up with "Pakistanis, Somalis, all of these African problems with violent Africans," Hanson said it started with the end of the White Australia Policy.

The postwar wave of migrants was different to today's situation because the new arrivals "really assimilated' and "learned to speak English", she said.

Hanson also suggested migrants were often coming to Australia "purely for the welfare system", claiming Australian Muslims were having children because the Quran taught "Allah will provide".

She said people were coming to Australia to take advantage of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), saying people from "Muslim areas" were "ripping the system off".

She said "a lot" of the scheme's nearly 800,000 participants came from those communities, but offered no evidence for the claim.

"But there’s a lot of Aussies too," she added. "So I’m not just going to pick them out, but it is quite known that in the Muslim streets you’ve got quite a lot in that street who are on the NDIS scheme."

Hanson has previously called for a " monocultural " society, saying multiculturalism in Australia has "failed".

During her first National Press Club address in June , she targeted the one in four Australians who speak other languages at home, saying it was impossible to generate social cohesion if people can't speak English.

Health and NDIS Minister Mark Butler said he was loath to respond to the podcast because Robinson was a convicted criminal who'd been disowned by leading figures on the right, but added he'd never seen a breakdown in nationality or religious background of NDIS participants.

"I'm not sure where Ms Hanson is getting her figures from, but they've never been provided to me ... I suspect they don't exist," he told ABC Radio National on Friday.

title.en: Trump Media to sell instant access to 'market-moving' social posts
title.zh: 特朗普媒体将出售关键社交帖子的早期访问权

summary.en: Trump Media is introducing a new service that offers Wall Street traders paid early access to its most influential social media posts.
summary.zh: 特朗普媒体公司将推出一项新服务，为华尔街交易员提供付费的早期访问权限，以获取其最具影响力的社交媒体帖子。

body.en:
Trump Media & Technology Group, which owns Truth Social, is launching a paid service to give Wall Street firms high-speed access to its most influential posts.

From 1 August, instant updates will be delivered from "the highest-ranking" accounts, it said. US President Donald Trump currently has the most followers on the platform.

The company behind the app hopes it will create a steady new source of money for the firm which is currently loss-making.

It is likely to be aimed at financial traders who want to see market-moving news fast. Trump’s social media posts often cause sudden swings in global markets, especially when he writes about trade and tariffs.

For firms, a delay of even seconds can be costly. Until now, banks and traders had to monitor the app manually. The new system will send posts directly to paying clients.

"Markets already move on Truth Social posts," said Kevin McGurn, the interim boss of Trump Media, adding that the service will create a steady profit.

The new commercial data feed, named Truth API, promises to deliver posts to paying institutional clients in "milliseconds".

The company, which launched its social media app in 2022, said some firms have been copying its data for months without permission.

McGurn warned that Trump Media will soon block these methods, forcing firms to buy the official feed instead.

Trump could benefit substantially from the move. Since his family remains the majority shareholder in the company, the president stands to profit directly from selling expedited access to his own public statements.

The BBC has contacted Trump Media for comment on whether or not the president's posts will be included in the paid feed. The White House declined to comment.

While other social media networks already sell data, the move highlights the unique overlap between Trump’s private businesses and his public role as president.

It would be "unprecedented" if the feature did include the president's posts, said Mark Spiegel, an investment expert from Stanphyl Capital Management.

Companies that trade off the latest headlines would be "at a disadvantage" if they did not pay for quick access as they could miss out on posts that could move markets, Spiegel said.

"But to put this in context, remember that Trump's posts constitute just a tiny fraction of what moves markets," he added.

Robert Frenchman, a partner at US law firm Dynamis, told Reuters: "It certainly does not seem fair, but yes, a tech platform can tier its distribution of information without violating federal securities laws."
body.zh: 拥有 Truth Social 的特朗普媒体与科技集团正在推出一项付费服务​​，让华尔街公司能够快速访问其最具影响力的帖子。 据称，从 8 月 1 日起，“排名最高”的账户将提供即时更新。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普目前在该平台上拥有最多的追随者。 该应用程序背后的公司希望能为目前亏损的公司创造一个稳定的新资金来源。 它可能是针对那些希望快速了解市场动态新闻的金融交易者。特朗普的社交媒体帖子经常引起全球市场的突然波动，尤其是当他撰写有关贸易和关税的文章时。 对于公司来说，即使是几秒钟的延迟也可能付出高昂的代价。到目前为止，银行和交易员必须手动监控该应用程序。新系统将直接向付费客户发送帖子。 特朗普媒体临时老板凯文·麦格恩表示，“市场已经开始关注真相社交帖子”，并补充说该服务将创造稳定的利润。 新的商业数据源名为 Truth API，承诺在​​“毫秒”内向付费机构客户发送帖子。 该公司于 2022 年推出了社交媒体应用程序，表示一些公司几个月来一直在未经许可的情况下复制其数据。 麦格恩警告说，特朗普媒体很快就会阻止这些方法，迫使公司转而购买官方饲料。 特朗普可能会从此举中获益匪浅。由于他的家族仍然是公司的大股东，总统可以通过出售他自己的公开声明的快速访问权来直接获利。 BBC 已联系特朗普媒体，请其就总统的帖子是否包含在付费视频中发表评论。白宫拒绝发表评论。 虽然其他社交媒体网络已经出售数据，但此举凸显了特朗普的私营企业与他作为总统的公共角色之间的独特重叠。 斯坦菲尔资本管理公司(Stanphyl Capital Management)的投资专家马克·斯皮格尔(Mark Spiegel)表示，如果该专题确实包含总统的帖子，那将是“前所未有的”。 斯皮格尔表示，如果不为快速访问付费，那些以最新头条新闻为代价的公司将“处于不利地位”，因为他们可能会错过可能影响市场的帖子。 “但要考虑到这一点，请记住，特朗普的帖子仅占推动市场的一小部分，”他补充道。 美国Dynamis律师事务所合伙人罗伯特·弗兰奇曼(Robert Frenchman)对路透社表示：“这看起来当然不公平，但确实，科技平台可以在不违反联邦证券法的情况下分级信息分发。”

reflection.en: This news highlights how information, especially influential content, can become a commodity where access is determined by wealth. Proverbs 11:1 reminds us that Yahweh values fairness and integrity in all commercial dealings, contrasting "dishonest scales" with "accurate weights." It challenges us to consider whether systems that grant privileged access...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了信息，特别是具有影响力的内容，如何成为一种商品，其获取取决于财富。箴言11:1提醒我们，雅伟看重所有商业交易中的公平和正直，将“不诚实的秤”与“准确的砝码”作对比。它挑战我们思考，那些基于付费提供特权访问的系统是否真正体现了公平的精神。

verse.textEn: Yahweh detests dishonest scales, but accurate weights find favor with him.
verse.textZh: 诡诈的天平为雅伟所憎恶；公平的法码为他所喜悦。

title.en: Why one man's dismissal has triggered rare wartime protests in Ukraine
title.zh: 为何一人被免职在乌克兰引发了罕见的战时抗议

summary.en: Mykhailo Fedorov, a 35-year-old tech expert, has been removed from his position as Ukraine's defense minister following an unexpected government reshuffle, a decision that has led to rare wartime protests.
summary.zh: 35岁的技术专家米哈伊洛·费多罗夫在一次意外的政府改组后被免去乌克兰国防部长的职务，这一决定引发了战时罕见的抗议活动。

body.en:
When 35-year-old Mykhailo Fedorov was appointed Ukraine's defence minister, he was the youngest ever to hold the position. Just six months later, his removal has sparked protests across Ukraine.

The former tech entrepreneur's departure came amid a surprise government reshuffle announced by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy this week that also included the dismissal of Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko.

Fedorov's removal was viewed as the result of infighting inside Ukraine's military establishment between Fedorov and Oleksandr Syrsky, commander-in-chief of Ukraine's armed forces.

Federov oversaw the defence ministry during a period in which Ukraine reversed some of Russia's battlefield momentum.

He said he had declined an offer from Zelenskyy to serve as an adviser after the president refused to include him in the next government.

Yevgeniy Khmara, head of Ukraine's SBU security service, has been appointed acting defence minister.

Fedorov had a reputation as a young, innovative moderniser who sought to reform the Ukrainian military. He has championed the use of advanced technology to fend off Russian attacks, becoming the public face of the country's popular drone program.

Before becoming defence minister, he served as Ukraine's minister of digital transformation and a close technology adviser to Zelenskyy.

He was the last remaining minister to have held positions in all of Zelenskyy's governments, having stayed close to the president since his election in 2019.

His supporters credited him with helping to slow Russia's advances this year , in part through his push to ramp up long-range drone strikes, cut bureaucracy, and use a data-driven approach to the war effort.

He also boosted military salaries and, before becoming defence minister, introduced computer game-like reward systems that allowed drone teams to earn rewards for striking Russian targets.

Earlier this year, Fedorov, who has close ties to Silicon Valley executives, negotiated an agreement with billionaire Elon Musk that saw Russia lose access to the Starlink satellite internet service on the battlefield.

Fedorov's push to modernise the military was rumoured to have caused friction with parts of the establishment.

Speaking to reporters following the reshuffle this week, both Fedorov and Zelenskyy effectively confirmed those suspicions.

Fedorov said he had a dispute with Syrsky, accusing the army chief of blocking the defence ministry's initiatives and dividing the country.

He criticised slow bureaucracy and a lack of flexibility, questioning whether Ukraine could defeat Russia with Syrsky in charge of the army.

title.en: School bus crash kills at least 20 pupils in Uganda
title.zh: 乌干达校车事故致至少20名学生死亡

summary.en: A school bus crash in Uganda resulted in the deaths of at least 20 pupils and injuries to dozens of others, including school staff. A mechanical fault is suspected as the cause of the accident.
summary.zh: 乌干达发生一起校车事故，造成至少20名学生死亡，包括学校工作人员在内的数十人受伤。事故原因疑为机械故障。

body.en:
At least 20 students and one adult have been killed after a bus carrying pupils on a study trip crashed in eastern Uganda, local officials say, in one of the country's deadliest road accidents involving children in recent years.

Dozens of others, including staff, were injured in the crash in Kapchorwa area on Thursday evening.

Preliminary investigations show the bus suffered a mechanical fault before the driver lost control on Chekwatit Hill, a stretch of road that has been the site of several serious crashes, according to local officials.

"The driver reportedly lost control of the vehicle, which veered off the road, struck a large stone along the roadside, and overturned," police said.

The bus, carrying pupils from King David Junior School in Ndejje, crashed at about 20:00 local time (17:00 GMT) at Chekwatit village in Kawowo area, police said.

"Sadly, 20 children and 1 adult, who happens to be the founder and director, Mr Tadeo Ssekade, have gone to be with the Lord," Minister of Local Government, Balaam Ateenyi Barugahara posted on X, while at the scene.

Videos shared by eyewitnesses showed the bus badly damaged, as local residents rushed to help the injured children.

The pupils were returning from a study tour, with local media reporting they had visited the Sipi Falls, a tourist area.

Uganda records thousands of road deaths every year, with speeding, poorly maintained vehicles and dangerous roads among the leading causes, according to traffic authorities.

The latest crash comes amid renewed concern over the safety of school transport after several serious bus accidents were reported in the country in recent weeks.
body.zh: 当地官员称，一辆载有学生前往学习旅行的巴士在乌干达东部发生车祸，造成至少 20 名学童和一名成人死亡，这是该国近年来涉及儿童的最严重的交通事故之一。 周四晚上，卡普乔瓦地区发生的车祸造成包括学校工作人员在内的数十人受伤。 据当地官员称，初步调查显示，这辆公交车在司机在切克瓦蒂特山(Chekwatit Hill)失控之前遭遇了机械故障，这条路曾发生过几起严重车祸。 警方表示：“据报道，司机失去了对车辆的控制，车辆偏离了道路，撞上了路边的一块大石头，然后翻了车。” 警方称，这辆载有恩代杰国王大卫小学学生的巴士于当地时间 20:00 左右（格林尼治标准时间 17:00）在卡沃沃地区的 Chekwatit 村坠毁。 当地政府部长 Balaam Ateenyi Barugahara 在现场时在 X 上发帖称：“遗憾的是，20 名儿童和 1 名成人（恰好是创始人兼董事 Tadeo Ssekade 先生）已经与主同在。” 目击者分享的视频显示，巴士严重受损，当地居民赶忙帮助受伤的孩子。 学生们刚刚结束游学归来，当地媒体报道称他们参观了旅游区西皮瀑布。 据交通部门称，乌干达每年都会记录数千人死于道路交通事故，其中超速行驶、车辆维护不善和道路危险是主要原因。 最近几周，该国发生了几起严重的公交车事故，人们对学校交通的安全再次产生了担忧，这起最新的事故发生之际。

reflection.en: The tragic loss of young lives in this accident brings profound sorrow and reminds us of the fragility of life. In moments of such deep grief, we hold onto the promise that Yahweh will one day wipe away every tear, and death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more. This hope anchors us even when our hearts are heavy with loss.
reflection.zh: 这起事故中年轻生命的悲惨逝去带来了深切的悲痛，提醒我们生命的脆弱。在如此深重的悲伤时刻，我们紧紧抓住雅伟的应许：有一天他将擦去所有的眼泪，死亡、悲哀、哭号和疼痛都将不再有。即使我们心中充满失落，这份盼望也能成为我们的锚。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: 'Shocking vulnerabilities': Trump makes sweeping claims China meddled in US elections
title.zh: “令人震惊的漏洞”：特朗普就中国干预美国大选发表全面声明

summary.en: The US president made broad election security claims, laying groundwork for the federal government to take action.
summary.zh: 美国总统就选举安全问题发表了广泛声明，为联邦政府采取行动奠定了基础。

body.en:
In a speech attacking US election integrity on Friday, US President Donald Trump released intelligence that he said showed major Chinese interference in US elections, reviving his false claims he won the 2020 election.

Trump's allegations about the "shocking vulnerabilities" in the American electoral system appeared to lay the groundwork for the Republican to dispute the results of November's crucial US midterm elections .

It underscored Trump's effort to make election security a central political issue ahead of November's midterm vote, when Republicans in Congress will face the prospect of losing control of both the House of Representatives and Senate — an outcome that would carry significant political consequences for Trump.

"We can never watch a stolen election again," Trump said in the primetime address, referencing his 2020 presidential election defeat by Democrat Joe Biden.

Trump said he was declassifying huge amounts of intelligence data that showed, among other things, that superpower rival China had illicitly acquired 220 million US voter files.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Over a period of years, starting during the 2020 election cycle, the People's Republic of China carried out what is believed to be the largest compromise of election data in history," Trump said in the televised speech from the White House.

He asserted that members of the US intelligence community deliberately suppressed information about the extent of China's activities.

His allegations contradict an unclassified 2021 US intelligence community assessment that found no indications any foreign actor tried to alter or succeeded in altering "any technical aspect" of the 2020 presidential election vote.

The assessment was conducted under John Ratcliffe, then Trump's director of national intelligence and now his CIA director.

Trump also claimed there were more than 250,000 non-US citizens registered to vote in four states.

Trump has persistently claimed his 2020 election defeat was "rigged," although more than 60 lawsuits produced no ruling establishing fraud capable of changing the outcome, while recounts, audits and his own justice department found none.

After railing against election security in the 25-minute address, Trump pressed Republicans in Congress to pass his signature elections legislation, the SAVE America Act, which has been stalled for months.

body.en:
Iran and the United States have exchanged intensifying fire in a week-long escalation that has largely unravelled last month's truce .

Iran has also disputed US President Donald Trump's claim that a US citizen who had been detained in Iran since 2024 had been released.

For the first time since a memorandum of understanding paused fighting last month, the US launched two large waves of airstrikes in a single day on Wednesday, mostly on targets near Iran's southern coast, and kept firing on Thursday.

In a statement, the US Central Command ⁠said US forces began "a new wave of strikes against Iran for the sixth consecutive night to further degrade Iranian military capabilities" on Friday.

Iran has countered with missiles and drones targeted at US military bases in neighbouring states, including a barrage at a recently expanded air base in Jordan.

After Iran resumed its blockade of the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, the US again blockaded Iranian ports from Wednesday.

The US military said it fired on a tanker near Iran's Kharg Island, with Hellfire missiles hitting its smokestack.

On Thursday, US projectiles struck Qeshm Island and near Bandar Abbas — home to Iran's largest port and key navy and Revolutionary Guards facilities — both on the Strait of Hormuz. Several locations in Bandar Abbas were hit by projectiles, the semi-official Mehr news agency reported, attributing the attack to the "American enemy."

Iran has signalled it could prod its Houthi allies in Yemen to close another key strait : the Bab al-Mandeb at the mouth of the Red Sea. Sources told Reuters Iran had already instructed the Houthis to shut it if the US carried out threats to attack Iran's infrastructure.

The week of increasingly intense exchanges has tested the boundaries of the restraint both sides largely observed during four months of fighting before last month's truce. Yet even as the attacks escalated, Trump on Wednesday welcomed what he described as the release of a US citizen detained in Iran, identified by a human rights lawyer as Dena Karari, calling it a gesture of goodwill by Iran.

On Thursday, however, Iran's judiciary challenged that account, saying no American prisoner had been released or exchanged from Iranian prisons, according to state media.

The US has said, however, that Iranian representatives were open to making a deal.

title.en: Why Gulf states are investing billions in Africa
title.zh: 海湾国家为何在非洲投资数十亿美元

summary.en: Wealthy Gulf states are investing billions in African countries, each with different strategic and economic objectives. The story explores the motivations behind these investments and their potential implications for African nations.
summary.zh: 富裕的海湾国家正在非洲国家投资数十亿美元，各国都有不同的战略和经济目标。这篇报道探讨了这些投资背后的动机及其对非洲国家的潜在影响。

body.en:
Wealthy Gulf states are investing billions in African countries. But the nations involved all have different objectives. What's behind the investments and what's in it for African countries?

The news came out just a few days ago: ADNOC Distribution, a petroleum retailer in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the  United Arab Emirates , will take over energy giant Shell's petrol stations and fuel business in South Africa. The price is thought to be around $1 billion (€870 million). With this purchase Abu Dhabi has assured itself of a place in the African continent's fuel market.

This billion-dollar deal is just one example of a larger trend. Even taking into account the occasional small declines, the Gulf states have been growing their economic presence in Africa for years now.

According to the UK-based think tank Chatham House, the countries belonging to the Gulf Cooperation Council or GCC, have invested more than $100 billion in Africa over the past decade. Around $59 billion of that came from the UAE and another $26 billion from Saudi Arabia .

"For the Gulf states, Africa isn't some far away region — it's right in their neighborhood," said Stephan Roll, a senior fellow in the Africa and Middle East division at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs. In eastern Africa, there are central trade routes and the two regions have had social and economic ties for decades. nobody should be surprised by the Gulf states' increasing engagement in Africa, he told DW.

"One of the biggest reasons why they started to look at Africa differently, especially over the past 10 years or so, has been the need to diversify away from hydrocarbons and also strengthen their own economic projection," Maddalena Procopio, a senior policy fellow in the Africa program at the European Council on Foreign Relations, explained. "But they started to also see the rest of Africa as an incredible potential market, where they could basically have revenues in sectors that they haven't ventured into."

According to analyses by a number of institutions, including the Brookings Institution, Chatham House and the African Development Bank Group, investment from out of the Gulf is focused on energy, ports, logistics, agriculture and critical raw materials. These investments make sense as they secure trade routes, strengthen food security and ensure access to raw materials like cooper, cobalt and lithium, which are needed for the development of electric vehicles and artificial intelligence.

The countries involved are pursuing different strategies though. Saudi Arabia and the UAE are mainly investing in renewable energies and in the processing and distribution of petroleum products, Procopio noted. Qatar , which has played a less significant role in Africa up until now,...

title.en: Monaco assassination plot takes a new turn
title.zh: 摩纳哥暗杀阴谋出现新进展

summary.en: A woman suspected in an assassination plot against a Ukrainian-Cypriot businessman in Monaco has been found dead in Ukraine, leading to the arrest of two men with ties to Ukraine's intelligence services.
summary.zh: 一名涉嫌在摩纳哥策划暗杀一名乌克兰裔塞浦路斯商人的女子在乌克兰被发现死亡，两名与乌克兰情报部门有联系的男子已被拘留。

body.en:
A woman suspected of plotting to assassinate a Ukrainian-Cypriot businessman in Monaco has been found dead in Ukraine. Two men with ties to Ukraine's intelligence services have now been brought into custody.

On July 7, the body of 39-year-old Ukrainian national Anastasia Berezovska was found near Kyiv. She was suspected of plotting an assassination attempt against Ukrainian-Cypriot businessman Vadym Yermolaiev , who is originally from the city of Dnipro, in Monaco.

A few days later, two men with ties to Ukraine's intelligence services were arrested on suspicion of killing Berezovska. What is known about the case, which could result in life sentences for the suspects and trigger an international scandal for Ukraine ?

Prosecutors in Monaco believe Berezovska attempted to kill Yermolaiev, his partner and their 13-year-old son. All three were injured when an explosive device detonated on the evening of June 29.

After reviewing surveillance footage, investigators concluded that Berezovska had monitored the victims over an extended period of time. She eventually placed a backpack containing explosives at the entrance to their home. The device was detonated remotely using a cellphone. Immediately afterward, she left the French Riviera. On July 6, her body was found in a forest near Kyiv.

Berezovska lived with her son in Hofheim, near Frankfurt, Germany. After fleeing Ukraine, she was granted temporary protection in Germany. According to a relative, she and her son lived modestly, relied on social benefits and were learning German.

Before moving to Germany , Berezovska had spent her entire life in Ukraine, first in the village of Horodyshche, where her mother still lives, and later in the city of Zhytomyr. Little is known about her professional background.

A relative told reporters that about a week before the assassination attempt, Anastasia Berezovska sent her 7-year-old son to stay with her mother in Ukraine. She herself apparently drove south from the Frankfurt metropolitan area. According to the news outlet Nice-Matin , traffic cameras captured her driving near the scene of the attack on June 26.

Immediately after the explosion, Berezovska left the French Riviera and returned to the Frankfurt region the following day. She did not stay there for long. On July 1, she crossed into Ukraine by bus and traveled to her mother's home in the village of Horodyshche.

Meanwhile, investigators in Monaco spotted a person wearing a dark suit in surveillance footage. They suspected it was a woman disguised as a man. After reviewing additional video recordings, suspicion fell on a heavily built woman with a snake tattoo on her shoulder. body.zh: 一名涉嫌密谋在摩纳哥刺杀一名乌克兰裔塞浦路斯商人的妇女在乌克兰被发现死亡。两名与乌克兰情报部门有联系的男子现已被拘留。 7月7日，39岁的乌克兰国民阿纳斯塔西娅·别列佐夫斯卡的尸体在基辅附近被发现。她涉嫌策划暗杀乌克兰裔塞浦路斯商人瓦迪姆·耶尔莫拉耶夫（Vadym Yermolaiev），他来自摩纳哥第聂伯罗市。 几天后，两名与乌克兰情报部门有联系的男子因涉嫌杀害别列佐夫斯卡而被捕。对于这起可能导致嫌疑人被判处无期徒刑并引发乌克兰国际丑闻的案件，我们了解多少？ 摩纳哥检察官认为别列佐夫斯卡试图杀死耶尔莫拉耶夫、他的伴侣以及他们 13 岁的儿子。 6 月 29 日晚，爆炸装置爆炸，三人全部受伤。 在查看监控录像后，调查人员得出结论，别列佐夫斯卡长期监视受害者。她最终将一个装有炸药的背包放在他们家的入口处。该装置是使用手机远程引爆的。紧接着，她就离开了法国里维埃拉。 7月6日，她的尸体在基辅附近的森林中被发现。 别列佐夫斯卡和她的儿子住在德国法兰克福附近的霍夫海姆。逃离乌克兰后，她在德国获得了临时保护。据一位亲戚说，她和儿子生活简朴，靠社会福利生活，正在学习德语。 在搬到德国之前，别列佐夫斯卡在乌克兰度过了一生，首先是在她母亲仍然居住的霍罗迪什切村，后来又搬到了日托米尔市。人们对她的专业背景知之甚少。 一位亲戚告诉记者，在暗杀事件发生前大约一周，阿纳斯塔西娅·别列佐夫斯卡将她7岁的儿子送到乌克兰与母亲住在一起。她本人显然是从法兰克福大都市区开车向南的。据新闻媒体《尼斯晨报》报道，6 月 26 日，交通摄像头拍到她在袭击现场附近开车的画面。 爆炸发生后，别列佐夫斯卡立即离开法国里维埃拉，并于第二天返回法兰克福地区。她并没有在那里停留太久。 7月1日，她乘坐巴士进入乌克兰，前往Horodyshche村母亲的家。 与此同时，摩纳哥的调查人员在监控录像中发现一名身穿深色西装的人。他们怀疑这是一个女扮男装的人。在查看了更多视频记录后，嫌疑人落在了一名身材魁梧、肩膀上有蛇纹身的女人身上。她所使用的汽车位于德国，当晚晚些时候，德国黑森州的警方进行了搜查……

reflection.en: This story of a complex assassination plot reminds us that not all conflicts are simple human disagreements. title.en: Why America's hospitals keep looking to India for nurses
title.zh: 美国医院为何持续从印度引进护士

summary.en: Thousands of nurses from India are seeking employment in the United States to address a growing shortage in the healthcare workforce. They face lengthy visa processing times, often waiting years to fulfill their aspirations.
summary.zh: 数千名印度护士渴望在美国工作，以填补日益增长的医疗劳动力短缺。她们需要应对长达数年的签证积压。

body.en:
Thousands of Indian nurses aspire to work in the US, navigating yearslong visa backlogs to fill a growing healthcare workforce shortage.

Angel Verghese, 25, has a clear plan. The nursing graduate from Welcare College of Nursing in Kochi in southern India's Kerala state has already passed the NCLEX, the US licensing exam for registered nurses.   

She is now gaining the work experience she needs before taking the IELTS English-language test and, she hopes, moving to New York, where her brother has already settled.

"I've always wanted to work in the US," Verghese told DW. "It offers better opportunities to learn, grow professionally and build a future. I know the process takes time, but I'm willing to wait."

Nearly 100 kilometers (62 miles) away in Kottayam, 26-year-old Susan Kurian is further along the same journey.

Having completed the clinical experience that US employers require, she is working with a recruitment agency to complete credential verification and secure a job offer from an American hospital.

"The paperwork is long and complicated, but my goal hasn't changed," Kurian told DW. "The US is where I want to build my career. I hope everything falls into place."

For thousands of young nurses across Kerala, the US remains the ultimate destination. The journey is rarely quick, often involving years of exams, paperwork and waiting, but the promise of better pay, career growth and international experience continues to draw them.

That demand is being fuelled by an American healthcare system struggling to find enough staff .

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects 189,100 registered nurse openings every year between 2024 and 2034, driven by an aging population and a wave of retirements.

Hospitals continue to recruit internationally, and India has become an increasingly important source of trained healthcare professionals.

Because Indian applicants face one of the longest employment-based immigration backlogs , nurses beginning the process today may have to wait more than a decade before receiving a US immigrant visa .

"Yes, we continue processing applications," Louie Terence, operations manager at Tiju's Academy, which prepares healthcare professionals for overseas licensing and language exams, told DW.

"Kerala nurses are well trained, speak good English and are known for their dedication. Many still see the US as the dream destination because of the salaries, working conditions and long-term career opportunities," said Terence.

Rather than waiting idle, many nurses begin the immigration process early. Recruitment agencies help them pass the NCLEX examination, complete credential verification and secure job offers from sponsoring US hospitals.

title.en: Trump alleges China meddled in 2020 election and questions voting security ahead of midterms
title.zh: 特朗普在中期选举前指控美国选举安全存在“令人震惊的漏洞”

summary.en: The president has made claims about China's interference in the 2020 US election, which contradict previous findings from US intelligence agencies. These allegations come as the country prepares for upcoming midterm elections.
summary.zh: 总统声称中国干预了2020年美国大选，这与美国情报机构此前的调查结果直接矛盾。这些指控是在该国准备中期选举之际提出的。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has delivered a primetime address in which he accused China of interfering in the 2020 election and alleged "shocking vulnerabilities" in American voting systems.

Trump, who spoke from the White House on Thursday, has repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims about voter fraud and foreign meddling in the 2020 election, which he lost to Joe Biden.

In the half-hour speech, delivered three months before the midterm elections, he said he had declassified hundreds of intelligence files which supported his claims that Beijing had tried to sway the election in Biden's favour.

The US intelligence community has previously concluded China did not interfere in the 2020 election.

In response to his speech, China's foreign ministry strongly denied the allegations of Chinese meddling in the 2020 presidential election, saying they were "entirely fabricated".

Trump's claims are "malicious smears" which have "long been proven to be groundless", foreign ministry spokesman Lin Jian said.

Trump spoke in front of several members of his top team as he gave his address, but journalists were unable to put questions to the president.

In his remarks, he accused China of the "illicit acquisition" of 220 million voter files including personal information.

Trump said voter data in 18 states was "bought, stolen or hacked by China" and accused "those responsible for sounding the alarm" of not disclosing the discovery to government officials or Congress.

Trump did not in his speech present any evidence that China had used the information it allegedly gathered to alter voting systems or to influence election outcomes.

Hundreds of pages of intelligence documents were released by the White House during Trump's address, many of them heavily redacted. The BBC is in the process of reviewing them.

Democrats, meanwhile, accused Trump of attempting to sow doubts about the security of the upcoming November midterms which will decide control of Congress for the remainder of his presidency.

"Let's be clear - in America, voters choose their leaders, not the other way around," top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer posted on social media after the speech.

"Democrats will fight like hell to make sure every American voter can cast their ballot freely, without obstruction or interference from Donald Trump," he added.

The president's comments contradict previous US intelligence assessments. A 2021 report by the US National Intelligence Council said it had "high confidence" that China did not interfere in the 2020 presidential election.

"We assess that China did not deploy interference efforts and considered but did not deploy influence efforts intended to change the outcome of the US presidential election," the report stated.

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普发表黄金时段讲话，指责中国干涉 2020 年大选，并声称美国投票系统存在“令人震惊的漏洞”。 周四在白宫发表讲话的特朗普多次就选民欺诈和外国干预 2020 年大选提出未经证实的指控，但他输给了乔·拜登。 在中期选举前三个月发表的半小时演讲中，他表示，他已经解密了数百份情报文件，这些文件支持他的说法，即北京试图影响选举，让选举有利于拜登。 美国情报界此前得出结论，中国没有干预2020年大选。 特朗普在发表讲话时在其高层团队的几名成员面前发表了讲话，但记者无法向总统提问。 他在讲话中指责中国“非法获取”包括个人信息在内的2.2亿份选民档案。 特朗普表示，18个州的选民数据“被中国购买、窃取或黑客入侵”，并指责“那些负责发出警报的人”没有向政府官员或国会披露这一发现。 特朗普没有提供证据证明中国利用其据称收集的信息来改变投票制度或影响选举结果。 作为对他讲话的回应，中国驻华盛顿大使馆告诉路透社，北京“从来没有也永远不会干预总统选举”。 BBC已联系中国外交部征求评论。 与此同时，民主党人指责特朗普试图对即将到来的 11 月中期选举的安全性产生怀疑，这次中期选举将决定他在总统任期剩余时间内对国会的控制权。 “让我们明确一点——在美国，选民选择他们的领导人，而不是相反，”参议院民主党领袖查克·舒默在演讲后在社交媒体上发帖称。 他补充说：“民主党人将竭尽全力确保每个美国选民都能自由投票，而不受唐纳德·特朗普的阻挠或干涉。” 总统的评论与美国之前的情报评估相矛盾。美国国家情报委员会2021年的一份报告称，“高度确信”中国没有干预2020年总统选举。 报告称：“我们评估认为，中国没有部署干预行动，并考虑过但没有部署旨在改变美国总统选举结果的影响力。” 报告称，这可能是因为中国“不认为任何一项选举结果都具有足够的优势，让中国在被抓到时冒着遭到反击的风险”。 特朗普在《华盛顿邮报》益普索公布的最新民意调查结果公布后发表了白宫讲话，该民意调查显示，许多选民对他的支持率已降至37%……

title.en: China hits out at British Steel nationalisation
title.zh: 中国抨击英国钢铁国有化

summary.en: The UK government announced the nationalization of British Steel, stating the move was to protect a crucial national capability. China subsequently expressed strong disapproval of this decision.
summary.zh: 英国政府宣布将英国钢铁公司收归国有，称此举旨在维护“一项重要的国家能力”。中国随后对此决定表示强烈不满。

body.en:
China has hit out at the nationalisation of British Steel, saying it "firmly opposes and is strongly dissatisfied with the British government's decision".

On Thursday, the UK government said that taking the loss-making firm into public hands would protect jobs and safeguard a "vital national capability".

The UK took control of British Steel's operations in Scunthorpe last year, though it was still owned by China's Jingye Group, limiting the government's ability to steer its future.

China's commerce ministry said on Friday that the moves "seriously infringed upon Jingye's legitimate rights and interests and severely undermined the confidence of Chinese companies investing in the UK".

It also called on Britain to "faithfully fulfil" its obligations under the China–UK Bilateral Investment Treaty.

"Disregarding Jingye's significant contribution to the UK economy and society, the British side forcibly took control of the company in the name of national security," the ministry said.

The statement added that Beijing would monitor developments closely and support Chinese firms to protect their rights, but did not specify what protecting Chinese companies' rights might involve.

The decision to nationalise British Steel threatens to strain the relationship between London and Beijing just as Andy Burnham is set to become the prime minister on Monday.

The incoming PM will have to weigh his approach to the issue with the economic benefits of ties with the world's second largest economy.

The China-UK Bilateral Investment Treaty is a legally binding agreement that was signed in 1986. It was designed to promote and protect investments between the two countries.

The nationalisation came after Parliament on Wednesday passed legislation allowing the government to bring the steel industry into public ownership under circumstances where it met a public interest test.

Jingye is seeking compensation, having previously said the business was losing £700,000 a day. The BBC has been unable to get a response from Jingye itself to Thursday's announcement.

By taking British Steel into public ownership the government now has the power and freedom to decide on the future of the plant, while keeping the blast furnaces going.

It is unlikely the government will want to continue running the business in the long term as it is costing it more than a million pounds a day.

In March, the National Audit Office said the Scunthorpe steelworks was costing the government about £1.3m a day.

Business Secretary Peter Kyle told the BBC the government would need to cover the running costs "for the immediate future".

The steelworks directly employs around 2,700 people in Scunthorpe as well as supporting thousands more jobs in the supply chain.

body.zh: 中方对英国钢铁公司国有化予以猛烈抨击，称“坚决反对，对英国政府的决定表示强烈不满”。 周四，英国政府表示，将这家亏损公司纳入公众手中将保护就业并维护“重要的国家能力”。 英国去年控制了英国钢铁公司在斯肯索普的业务，尽管该公司仍由中国敬业集团所有，这限制了政府掌控其未来的能力。 中国商务部周五表示，此举“严重侵犯敬业公司的合法权益，严重损害中国企业对英国投资的信心”。 它还呼吁英国“忠实履行”中英双边投资条约规定的义务。 英方无视敬业公司对英国经济社会的重大贡献，以国家安全为名，强行控制敬业公司。 声明补充说，北京将密切关注事态发展并支持中国企业保护自身权利，但没有具体说明保护中国企业权利可能涉及哪些内容。 就在安迪·伯纳姆将于周一就任英国首相之际，英国钢铁公司国有化的决定可能会导致伦敦和北京之间的关系紧张。 即将上任的总理必须权衡自己处理这一问题的方法与与世界第二大经济体建立联系的经济利益。 《中英双边投资条约》是1986年签署的具有法律约束力的协议，旨在促进和保护两国之间的投资。 周三，议会通过了一项立法，允许政府在满足公共利益要求的情况下将钢铁行业纳入公有制。 敬业正在寻求赔偿，此前曾表示该业务每天损失 70 万英镑。 BBC 尚未得到敬业本身对周四的公告的回应。 通过将英国钢铁公司纳入公有制，政府现在拥有决定工厂未来的权力和自由，同时保持高炉的运转。 从长远来看，政府不太可能继续经营该业务，因为每天的成本超过一百万英镑。 3 月份，国家审计办公室表示，斯肯索普钢铁厂每天给政府造成的损失约为 130 万英镑。 商务大臣彼得·凯尔告诉英国广播公司，政府需要“在不久的将来”承担运营成本。

title.en: Xi Jinping calls for international cooperation in AI development at WAIC in Shanghai
title.zh: 习近平在上海世界人工智能大会上呼吁加强人工智能国际合作

summary.en: Chinese President Xi Jinping attended the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai, where he outlined China's approach to AI diplomacy, aiming to challenge the United States' leadership in the artificial intelligence sector.
summary.zh: 中国国家主席习近平出席了在上海举行的世界人工智能大会（WAIC），他在会上阐述了中国的人工智能外交愿景，旨在挑战美国在该领域的主导地位。

body.en:
Xi Jinping marked his first in-person attendance at the World ​Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai, where he shared China's vision of AI diplomacy to challenge US dominance in the sector.

China's President Xi Jinping  has called for global cooperation on  artificial intelligence (AI)  development, telling a major Shanghai forum that no single country should dominate the AI industry.

Xi on Friday delivered a keynote address at the opening event of the World ​Artificial ‌Intelligence Conference (WAIC), which he was attending for the first time, underpinning AI's growing strategic importance for China.

"AI development should not be a solo performance by a single country, but a symphony of international cooperation," Xi said at the gathering.

To prevent the creation of what he called "new ​historical injustices" ​in AI, Xi promoted Beijing's role in ensuring equitable access for developing countries to AI capacity building.

He announced China's plans to cooperate with several international bodies, including from Asia, Africa, Latin America and BRICS  nations to provide opportunities in the AI domain.

On Thursday, representatives from 29 nations inked an agreement to establish ​the World AI Cooperation Organization, headquartered in Shanghai, China's Xinhua news agency reported.

The signatory nations included Russia, Belarus, ⁠Serbia, Cuba, Brazil and Venezuela, along with 12 Asian and 10 African countries.

China says the intergovernmental body aims to promote international cooperation and global ​governance in AI.

Xi also stressed the importance of a "people-centered" approach in the development of AI technology.

"We should put in place laws and regulations, technological monitoring, early warning, and emergency response systems, in order to ... ensure AI is always under human control," the Chinese leader said.

The conference comes as China and the United States prepare for their first government-level AI talks under US President Donald Trump's administration. 

Chinese AI models are attracting global users with lower costs as they catch up to the more expensive US AI offerings.

The United States and European Union have imposed curbs on tech imports from China, citing national security concerns.

There are also growing concerns over the deployment of AI on the battlefield and its use by hackers and terrorists.

"We should jointly oppose overstretching the national security concept in the field of AI or placing one country's security over that of others," Xi said on Friday.

The WAIC lasts for four days and features over 1,000 exhibitors from Chinese tech firms alongside officials and researchers.

title.en: 'Shocking vulnerabilities': Trump makes sweeping claims China meddled in US elections
title.zh: “令人震惊的漏洞”：特朗普就中国干预美国大选发表全面声明

summary.en: The US president made broad election security claims, laying groundwork for the federal government to take action.
summary.zh: 美国总统就选举安全问题发表了广泛声明，为联邦政府采取行动奠定了基础。

body.en:
In a speech attacking US election integrity on Friday, US President Donald Trump released intelligence that he said showed major Chinese interference in US elections, reviving his false claims he won the 2020 election.

Trump's allegations about the "shocking vulnerabilities" in the American electoral system appeared to lay the groundwork for the Republican to dispute the results of November's crucial US midterm elections .

It underscored Trump's effort to make election security a central political issue ahead of November's midterm vote, when Republicans in Congress will face the prospect of losing control of both the House of Representatives and Senate — an outcome that would carry significant political consequences for Trump.

"We can never watch a stolen election again," Trump said in the primetime address, referencing his 2020 presidential election defeat by Democrat Joe Biden.

Trump said he was declassifying huge amounts of intelligence data that showed, among other things, that superpower rival China had illicitly acquired 220 million US voter files.

Trump has persistently claimed his 2020 election defeat was "rigged," although more than 60 lawsuits produced no ruling establishing fraud capable of changing the outcome, while recounts, audits and his own justice department found none.

title.en: Philippines condemns monkey video on Chinese media as racist
title.zh: 菲律宾谴责中国媒体上的“猴子视频”为种族主义

summary.en: An AI-generated video circulated on Chinese media, depicting a monkey in Philippine attire singing about claims to the South China Sea, has been condemned by the Philippines as racist.
summary.zh: 中国媒体上流传的一段人工智能视频，展示了一只身着菲律宾服装的猴子演唱其对南海的主张，菲律宾谴责该视频具有种族主义色彩。

body.en:
The Philippines has condemned the "dehumanising and racist" portrayal of the country as a timid monkey strong-armed by the US and Japan to take Beijing on over the South China Sea .

Last week, China Daily posted an AI-generated video featuring a monkey in a Filipino shirt. It screams as arms bearing the Japanese and US flags shove it onto a rickety karaoke stage set up in a boat.

After it gets scolded for singing the wrong song, it pulls out a sheet reading "South China Sea arbitration award". It is then flung into the sea and blasted by a water cannon.

Tense stand-offs and occasional violent confrontations between Philippine and Chinese vessels in the disputed waters have grown in recent years.

At the centre of tensions between Manila and Beijing are the Spratly Islands and Scarborough Shoal (known as Huangyan Island in China), a little more than 100 miles (160km) from the Philippines and 500 miles from China.

The Chinese Coast Guard routinely uses high-pressure water cannons against Philippine vessels in the disputed shoals, which have led to damage and injuries.

"Disagreement over legal and political issues does not justify resorting to disturbing imagery, which has no place in the civil public discourse of a responsible state," Manila's foreign ministry said, demanding that the clip be removed.

"Such imagery and misinformation only serve to widen the distrust between the Philippines and China," it added.

The Philippine defence ministry called the video "contemptible propaganda", saying it "exposes the moral and intellectual bankruptcy of China's propaganda machine".

"The recent spate of schizophrenic behaviour of the Chinese Communist Party is too clear to disregard or ignore," defence secretary Gilbert Teodoro said.

The video, posted on 10 July, remains on China Daily's Facebook page at time of writing.

The past week marks a decade since the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague ruled in favour of the Philippines, concluding that China's expansive claims in the South China Sea had no legal basis under international law.

Tensions between Beijing and Manila have sharply escalated in recent years due to their overlapping claims, with each side accusing the other of provocations and altercations at sea, including some involving weapons such as swords, spears and knives.

In June, Beijing installed a floating barrier at the entrance to the Scarborough Shoal that was removed after the Philippines filed formal diplomatic protests.

Also in June, China barred Teodoro, Manila's defence secretary, and his immediate family from entering mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau.

China Daily's caption to its post of the monkey clip reiterates Bejing's position.

title.en: Hong Kong police raid two bookstores, arrest five people
title.zh: 香港警方突袭两家书店，逮捕五人

summary.en: Hong Kong police have arrested five booksellers and raided two independent bookstores, citing the sale of allegedly "seditious" publications. This action marks the latest step in an ongoing crackdown on independent bookshops in the city.
summary.zh: 香港警方逮捕了五名书商，并搜查了两家独立书店，理由是这些书店涉嫌销售“煽动性”出版物。此举是香港持续打击独立书店的最新行动。

body.en:
Five booksellers have been arrested in Hong Kong over the sale of allegedly "seditious" publications. Two bookstores have become the latest target in a continued crackdown on independent bookshops

Police in Hong Kong carried out raids on two bookshops, arresting five people under suspicion of displaying and selling seditious publications, reports said Wednesday.

The move marks a third round of arrests in a clampdown on independent bookstores, with similar operations conducted in March and June. 

The raids are widely seen as an attempt to crush free speech and dissent under the semi-autonomous city's stringent national security law .

According to media reports, police raided Have A Nice Stay bookshop —  founded by former journalists —  and Greenfield Book Store.

Footage shared by media outlets showed officers in vests marked with "Police" seizing boxes from  Have A Nice Stay while the AFP news agency said its reporters saw a woman in handcuffs being taken to the van from the store. 

Similar events were reported a few streets away, as boxes were carried out of the building that houses Greenfield Book Store, a video posted by  The Collective online news outlet showed.

A police statement later confirmed that two stores in Mong Kok district were raided, without naming the shops. 

The raid on Have A Nice Stay came a day after it announced in a Facebook post that it was shutting down on August  30, over reasons including "uncertainties regarding the social environment" and financial difficulties.

The police said the stores were searched by the National Security Department after customs officials alerted them to the discovery of allegedly seditious books in a shipment to Hong Kong from overseas.

The police statement said the publications' content included stirring up hatred against the city's government, judiciary and law enforcement agencies.

They said that the five people —  two men and three women —  were arrested on suspicion of violating the 2024 national security law.

The offense is punishable with up to seven years in prison under Hong Kong's national security law, which was enforced in 2024 on top of a 2020 legislation imposed by China after massive pro-democracy protests.

Hong Kong's independent bookstore industry once flourished, but it has dwindled since the enactment of the sweeping security law. 

In June, two employees of Hong Kong's Hunter bookstore were arrested, while four workers of the Book Punch were detained in March for selling "seditious" publications.

body.en:
University leaders have admitted that they failed to adequately protect Jewish students and staff from the psychological impact of pro-Palestinian protests on campuses, the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion has heard this week.

The commission today heard evidence an Australian National University student was asked to provide death certificates for relatives who were killed by Israeli forces.

Mary Russell, chief executive of the Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Authority, said she had heard of several instances where academics had not responded to students affected by Israel-Palestine tensions in a reasonable way.

Russell said while it was customary for universities to require proof before assessment changes were granted, there were "profound differences" in circumstances if family members died at the hands of the Israeli Defense Force or Hamas.

"The lack of trauma-informed and student-centred approaches... were so significant and important and so pervasive," she said.

Russell appeared on the final day of hearings into antisemitism and hate speech on university campuses with dozens of witnesses believing more could be done to protect staff and students.

Monash University professor David Slucki told the commission that universities had "pretty adequate" policies for protecting Jewish people on campuses, instead calling for broader conversations about university cultures.

"You don't legislate your way out of social discord. We actually need to find a way to change the cultures in our institutions," he said.

Slucki, who helped develop the Australian universities' definition of anti-Jewish hatred, said it was important to remember that understandings of Zionism - and therefore definitions of antisemitism - varied based on interpretation of history.

Australian National University's interim vice-chancellor Rebekah Brown apologised on Thursday that Jewish members did not feel safe as a long-running pro-Palestinian encampment was held at ANU in 2024.

However, staff and university leaders say they have had to grapple with the need for academic freedom of speech and that claims of antisemitism have diminished the right to protest.

Sydney University vice-chancellor Mark Scott said universities should be able to serve as "bastions of free speech" and that he has not bowed to pressure to ban pro-Palestinian protest slogans.

Universities and the higher education sector have been under the royal commission's microscope since Monday as it attempts to investigate the prevalence of antisemitic racism in Australian society.

body.en:
One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has drawn criticism for appearing on a podcast with controversial far-right UK activist Tommy Robinson, where she pointed to the scrapping of the White Australia policy as the root cause of migration issues in the country.

The nearly hour-long conversation, recorded last week during Hanson's visit to the UK, was published on Robinson's podcast on Friday.

The appearance has since drawn criticism from other politicians, though not everyone in Canberra has condemned it.

Between speaking about her scepticism about the COVID-19 vaccine, the potential for her daughter to eventually lead One Nation, and reflections on her time in prison and her burqa incidents in parliament , Hanson focused heavily on immigration.

Asked by Robinson how Australia had ended up with "Pakistanis, Somalis, all of these African problems with violent Africans," Hanson said it started with the end of the White Australia Policy.

The postwar wave of migrants was different to today's situation because the new arrivals "really assimilated' and "learned to speak English", she said.

Hanson also suggested migrants were often coming to Australia "purely for the welfare system", claiming Australian Muslims were having children because the Quran taught "Allah will provide".

She said people were coming to Australia to take advantage of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), saying people from "Muslim areas" were "ripping the system off".

She said "a lot" of the scheme's nearly 800,000 participants came from those communities, but offered no evidence for the claim.

"But there’s a lot of Aussies too," she added. "So I’m not just going to pick them out, but it is quite known that in the Muslim streets you’ve got quite a lot in that street who are on the NDIS scheme."

Hanson has previously called for a " monocultural " society, saying multiculturalism in Australia has "failed".

During her first National Press Club address in June , she targeted the one in four Australians who speak other languages at home, saying it was impossible to generate social cohesion if people can't speak English.

Health and NDIS Minister Mark Butler said he was loath to respond to the podcast because Robinson was a convicted criminal who'd been disowned by leading figures on the right, but added he'd never seen a breakdown in nationality or religious background of NDIS participants.

"I'm not sure where Ms Hanson is getting her figures from, but they've never been provided to me ... I suspect they don't exist," he told ABC Radio National on Friday.

body.en:
Telstra did not act on repeated warnings to fix an impending issue with a piece of equipment that ultimately triggered a devastating network outage, a parliamentary inquiry has heard.

United States-based supplier Microchip Technology warned the telco multiple times that a Network Time Protocol server required a software update to prevent a "rollover problem" that would take down the system, Telstra officials told a hearing in Canberra.

The snap inquiry was set up in response to the ensuing outage, which left train networks in disarray and customers unable to dial Triple Zero.

In a submission to the inquiry, the telco said a GPS card within the server did not operate as expected once power was restored to the device following scheduled maintenance.

The change had not been properly documented, meaning the maintenance team was not aware the issue would occur when the device was restarted.

A software update, which could have averted the outage, had also not been applied to the device.

An EFTPOS payment system used by about 80,000 businesses confirmed it had been impacted, with a number of customers taken offline and unable to process payments.

Train services had to be cancelled after severe network disruptions in both Victoria and NSW, triggering strong criticism from the federal government.

A Network Time Protocol (NTP) is a set of rules that govern timekeeping on a computer network. NTP is one of the oldest and most basic computer network protocols still in use today.

It was invented by legendary US computer engineer David Mills in 1985 to ensure that all computers on a given network were synchronised to Coordinated Universal Time (or UTC) within a margin of a few milliseconds. It has been heavily modified and updated over the years to encompass and incorporate new technologies and network infrastructures.

Mills' invention of the NTP was so groundbreaking that it earned him the nickname 'Father Time' among his peers.

This level of synchronisation is important, particularly when working with systems that use timekeeping as a central component — like train networks.

For instance, NTP allows computers on a network to coordinate their logging so that administrators and IT professionals can track error reports or security concerns in the precise chronological order they occurred, no matter where they happened in the network or the world.

It also ensures greater internet and network security and authentication. Many encryption methods depend on very strict time synchronisation to confirm real vs malicious traffic.

The federal government will establish an education taskforce aimed at tackling Islamophobia and training politicians and public servants as part of its response to the special envoy to combat Islamophobia's landmark report .

But SBS News understands the government will not endorse several of the 54 recommendations Aftab Malik put forward in his report handed to the prime minister 10 months ago, casting doubt from Muslim community leaders over the government's commitments to adequately tackle Islamophobia.

Malik called for a ban on religious discrimination, for Muslims to join Sikhs and Jews in being explicitly protected in existing racial discrimination laws, and an independent review into counterterrorism laws to investigate whether Muslims in Australia were discriminated against.

He also recommended the government set up a commission of inquiry into Islamophobia, as well as a separate inquiry into anti-Palestinian and anti-Arab racism, which he said increased as a result of the government's lack of "moral action" for Middle Eastern diaspora.

The government's response, expected to be released on Saturday, will outline other measures to help tackle the rise in anti-Muslim behaviour in the country.
